theme: 3 terms on collection protocols: a collection you can write into, one you can walk backward, and one where jumping to any index takes one step

terms.definition: A collection protocol that lets you change items in place through the subscript, for example with `swapAt`.
terms.example: `Array` is a MutableCollection, so sort it in place instead of making a copy.
terms.code:
var nums = [3, 1, 2]
nums[0] = 9        // write by index
nums.swapAt(0, 2)  // swap two items
print(nums)

terms.definition: A collection protocol that can step backward as well as forward, which gives you `last` and `reversed`.
terms.example: Make it generic over BidirectionalCollection, because we need `last`.
terms.code:
let word = "Swift"
let i = word.index(before: word.endIndex)
print(word[i])
print(String(word.reversed()))

terms.definition: A collection protocol that promises jumping to any index, or measuring the distance, takes one step.
terms.example: `String` isn't a RandomAccessCollection, so jumping to the middle is slow.

quizzes.question: Which collection protocol promises that jumping to any index takes one step?
In this code, which protocol lets `reset` write into the collection?
Which protocol adds stepping backward to a collection, so it can offer `last`?

video.title: Collection Protocols: Mutable, Bidirectional, RandomAccess | Day 67
video.description:
Learn to explain collection protocols in Swift: MutableCollection, BidirectionalCollection & RandomAccessCollection, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
MutableCollection - A collection protocol that lets you change items in place through the subscript, for example with `swapAt`.
BidirectionalCollection - A collection protocol that can step backward as well as forward, which gives you `last` and `reversed`.
RandomAccessCollection - A collection protocol that promises jumping to any index, or measuring the distance, takes one step.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift MutableCollection, BidirectionalCollection & RandomAccessCollection | Day 67
landscape.description:
Explain MutableCollection, BidirectionalCollection & RandomAccessCollection in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
MutableCollection, BidirectionalCollection, RandomAccessCollection 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

MutableCollection - A collection protocol that lets you change items in place through the subscript, for example with `swapAt`.
한국어: MutableCollection: 서브스크립트로 항목을 제자리에서 바꿀 수 있게 해 주는 컬렉션 프로토콜 (예: `swapAt`)

BidirectionalCollection - A collection protocol that can step backward as well as forward, which gives you `last` and `reversed`.
한국어: BidirectionalCollection: 앞뿐 아니라 뒤로도 이동할 수 있어 `last`와 `reversed`를 쓸 수 있는 컬렉션 프로토콜

RandomAccessCollection - A collection protocol that promises jumping to any index, or measuring the distance, takes one step.
한국어: RandomAccessCollection: 어떤 인덱스로 건너뛰거나 거리를 재는 일이 한 번에 끝난다고 약속하는 컬렉션 프로토콜

In this video, Mina and Jake find out why `last` was missing, why the middle lookup needs a stronger protocol and why an array can swap items but a string cannot, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: Why doesn't Collection have last? Can you explain it in English?

dialogue.title: Where did last go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `newest` used `Collection` first, and `last` wasn't there. Why?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A plain Collection only walks forward. `last` needs a BidirectionalCollection.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because it has to step back from the end?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. A BidirectionalCollection can move both ways, like `String` or `Array`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why is `middle` a RandomAccessCollection, not just bidirectional?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On a RandomAccessCollection, jumping with `offsetBy` takes one step.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And on a `String`, it would walk character by character?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. That's slow for long text.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last thing. Why can I call `swapAt` on `feed`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: `Array` is a MutableCollection, so you can change items in place.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. A `String` isn't a MutableCollection, so I can't swap its characters.
A MutableCollection lets you change items in place.
